messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: elevated error rate for private/on-prem connected customers in Azure northeurope (1769991111) — multiple prefixes observing DNS SERVFAIL and TCP/UDP 53 drops. Auto-create incident thread.

maria (oncall-sre): I see the pager. I'm taking initial lead. Observed 15% 5xxs for routes that egress via azure-northeurope.

aj (infra): confirming logs from our NAT gateways — spikes in UDP retransmits and some TCP resets on port 53. Looks like a network delivery issue upstream.

ben (netops): We're seeing route flap events between spoke vNets and vWAN hubs in northeurope. BGP session churn to Azure-managed transit appears correlated ~1769991000-1769991050.

maria (oncall-sre): Immediate impact: customers with Private (VPC/on-prem) VPNs or ExpressRoute loss of internal DNS resolution causing failed model routing and connection timeouts. SLO impact: increased tail latency and errors for private deployments.

tina (customer-success): I've got two customers on active pages: AcornHealth and AtlasPay — both report timeouts on inference calls since ~11:18 UTC. AcornHealth has production traffic failing on private endpoints.

sam (eng-runtime): Repro steps from on-prem: dig shows SERVFAIL to our internal forwarders: 
```
; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> @10.10.20.5 svc.platform.internal A +short
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
```
Also TCP 53 attempts get RSTs intermittently.

maria (oncall-sre): Triage plan: 1) Fail traffic to eu-west region for affected customers where cross-region routing allowed (temporary). 2) Engage Azure support for northeurope vWAN/BGP issue. 3) Short TTL DNS patch where possible, and 4) Keep customers informed.

ben (netops): I'm opening TAC with Azure now — uploading bgp and flow logs. Ticket: AZURE-TAC-987654. They acknowledged a platform-level routing recalculation causing transient packet drops in hub fabric.

ops-bridge-bot: Joined call bridge https://meet.redwood/ops/1769991111 — bridge created, pinning to thread.

maria (oncall-sre): Mitigation action 1: For AtlasPay (allowed), we hit canary policy to route their traffic to eu-west1 dedicated pool. Command run: `redwood route update --org atlaspay --region eu-west-1 --force-failover` — success, initial metrics show 95% reduction in 5xxs for that tenant. :thumbsup:

sam (eng-runtime): For customers that cannot cross-region, we can attempt local egress workaround: spin a transient NAT VM in northeurope, attach to alternate peer path, and SNAT their traffic there. I'll coordinate with infra.

aj (infra): Spinning nat-proxy-1769 (t2-medium) in northeurope, configuring SNAT and dns-forwarders to 10.10.20.6 — will route impacted subnets through it via UDR. ETA ~8m.

tina (customer-success): Messaging update to AcornHealth: "We're aware of DNS/resolution failures affecting private endpoints in Azure northeurope. We're performing failover actions and will update in 15m." They've acknowledged and will route lower-priority jobs to eu-west if stable.

ben (netops): Azure TAC says they're seeing an internal control-plane recalculation that caused vWAN route-programming inconsistencies between 11:12-11:22 UTC — they are rolling a fix; platform engineers pushing state sync. They requested we avoid BGP session restarts while they heal.

maria (oncall-sre): Observability checklist: 1) enable verbose dns tracing for affected tenants, 2) annotate traces with route decision, 3) preserve packet captures for TAC. I've enabled and saved pcap from nat-proxy-1769: /var/log/pcaps/northeurope-1769991111.pcap

sam (eng-runtime): Runtime note: when DNS fails for private endpoints some of our SDKs fall back to public egress which leaks internal hostnames — need a follow-up to enforce fail-hard policy. Capturing that as action item.

aj (infra): nat-proxy-1769 active, traffic diverted — initial telemetry shows DNS success rates for routed subnets up from 40% -> 92%. Good temporary fix.

maria (oncall-sre): Handoff: I need to go offline for 20m. @ben will own bridging with Azure TAC and infra for nat-proxy. @sam please continue runtime mitigations. I'll be reachable on DRI pager. Handoff note ID: HND-1769991300.

ben (netops): Taking ownership. I'll push updates to this thread and Azure TAC. If anything degrades we escalate to severity 1.

ops-bridge-bot: Incident severity set to P2 by maria — moving to monitoring.

(30m later) ben (netops): Azure reports control-plane rollout complete at 11:41 UTC. BGP flaps subsided. We observed residual packet drops that cleared by 11:46 after state converged.

tina (customer-success): All impacted customers contacted with interim report. AcornHealth confirmed recovery and no data loss; AtlasPay traffic stable on eu-west.

maria (oncall-sre): Closing notes: root cause seems to be an Azure vWAN route-programming race during an internal control-plane change which triggered transient route inconsistencies and DNS packet drops for hub egress. Mitigations used: targeted region failover, transient NAT proxy, and DNS TTL/trace captures.

maria (oncall-sre): Postmortem owners: netops (ben), infra (aj), runtime (sam), cs (tina). Target: initial incident summary in 24h and full postmortem in 72h.

incident-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring at 1769992460.

ben (netops): Will attach BGP dump, TAC transcript, and pcap to the incident ticket after I validate sanitization.

maria (oncall-sre): Thanks team. Stand down unless new regressions. :white_check_mark:
